 SBS names Kathryn Fink chief content officer in executive restructure
 Sean Slatter · News TV & Streaming · October 21, 2026 
 Kathryn Fink and Matthew Hancock. 
 SBS director of television Kathryn Fink will move into the expanded role of chief content officer as part of the broadcaster’s new executive structure, which will also elevate streaming and digital products general manager Matthew Hancock to director of digital.
 Fink, who joined SBS in July 2022, will lead a portfolio spanning television and online content, sport, NITV, audio and language content, digital, and marketing and audiences. SBS said the role would support more integrated planning and delivery across all platforms, including audio services in more than 60 languages.
 Hancock, who joined SBS in 2016 and has served as general manager of streaming and digital products since July 2024, will lead digital audience growth, product development and platform strategy, with a focus on continuing to innovate SBS On Demand. He will sit on the SBS executive team and report to Fink. Both roles are effective immediately.
 Also reporting to Fink are the director of audio and language content, a role Pamela Cook occupies in an acting capacity, and director of marketing and audiences, Uma Oldham. Both roles remain on the SBS executive team and have a dual reporting line to the managing director. Recruitment is currently underway for a new director of audio and language content.
 Rounding out the changes is the elevation of Stig Bell to chief people officer, after serving as SBS director of people and culture since August 2017 and initially joining the public broadcaster in 2013. His expanded remit spans the people and culture, inclusion, organisational capability and enterprise strategy functions.
 SBS managing director Jane Palfreyman, said the new structure was designed to support more integrated planning and closer collaboration as digital platforms reshaped how audiences discovered and engaged with content.
 “By bringing our people and expertise together across content and platforms, we can take SBS’s distinctive stories and services to more Australians, and help everyone feel part of the story of modern Australia,” she said.
 Fink said the new structure came at a time when SBS’s role in the country’s media landscape had never been more important.
 “Bringing our incredibly talented content, marketing and digital teams together will help audiences discover and engage with the stories and services that matter to them, wherever they choose to watch, listen or read,” she said. 
 “It’s a privilege to lead this work and continue delivering meaningful impact for communities across the country.”
